ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, officer, subscriber, shareholder and individual with significant control against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and Criminal Code listed terrorist entities. Enhanced due diligence is required for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates under FINTRAC guidance; source of wealth and source of funds must be verified, all controllers above the 25% threshold must be identified, and records must be retained for at least five years. Any suspicious transactions must be reported to FINTRAC without tipping-off.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre and NUANS Name Reservation System administered by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A federal corporate name may be in English, French, or both. The name must be expressed in roman script; accents used in English and French are permitted. Chinese characters or other non-roman script are not accepted in the legal corporate name. The legal element must be Limited, Incorporated, Corporation, or an accepted abbreviation such as Ltd., Inc., Corp., or Ltée. The name must be distinguishable from existing names in the NUANS database and must not be likely to confuse the public.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trust Company, Loan Company, Insurance, Assurance - federal financial-services reserved terms
Royal, Crown, Queen, King, Governor General, Government, Canada, Canadian - require evidence of lawful entitlement or government authorization
University, College, Institute - require prior approval from the educational regulator or establishing statute
Engineer, Engineering, Architect, Architecture - regulated professional titles requiring provincial consent
Lawyer, Barrister, Solicitor, Legal Services - Law Society of Ontario approval required
Accountant, Auditor, Chartered Professional Accountant - protected CPA designation and regulatory consent
Cooperative, Co-op, Society, Foundation - terms reserved for other statutory corporate forms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS-based reservation may be renewed for an additional 90 days by filing a renewal with Corporations Canada before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant may request reconsideration in writing from the Director under the Canada Business Corporations Act within 60 days of the refusal. If the Director maintains the refusal, judicial review may be filed in the Federal Court under section 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-7, within 30 days of the communication of the final decision. For Ontario extra-provincial registration, name objections and appeals are handled through ServiceOntario under the Corporations Information Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a federal corporation registered in Ontario provided the address is a physical street address in Ontario, is not merely a post-office box, and the commercial registered agent accepts service of process at that address. A virtual office arrangement is routinely accepted for low-risk standard businesses such as a specialty tea salon lounge, especially where the operational tea salon is located at a separate physical commercial premise.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for the registered office itself, estimated at 5-10% absent tax or AML red flags or filings irregularities. The operating tea-salon premise has a high likelihood of routine unannounced inspection by municipal public health and food-safety authorities once the food or beverage establishment is active.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Business Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16 (OBCA), as amended; applicable sections include s. 2 (application), s. 4 (constating documents), s. 5-6 (articles of incorporation), s. 8 (corporate names), s. 13 (registered office), s. 14 (by-laws), s. 17 (first directors), s. 19 (notice of directors), s. 20 (board powers), s. 93 (share subscription); alternatively, if federal incorporation is chosen, Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 7-9, 16-18, 106 and 114, with Ontario extra-provincial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Ontario, operating through the Ontario Business Registry (portal); alternative federal authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation filed electronically through the Ontario Business Registry; federal equivalent: ISED Form 4011 - Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an OBCA corporation; share capital may be authorized in any amount and consideration may be paid in cash, property, past services or contractual obligations; no escrow or blocked capital account is required under OBCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers listed in the Schedule of Share Subscriptions are hereby allotted and issued 100 Class A Common Shares of the Corporation in consideration of the capital contributions reflected in the books, and such issuance is accepted and ratified; FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Corporation be fixed at the address set out in the Articles of Incorporation in the Province of Ontario, and that the standard corporate by-law be adopted; FURTHER RESOLVED that [Name] shall hold office as President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer until successors are elected; and the officers are directed to open banking accounts, execute premises leases, procure insurance, and make all regulatory filings necessary to commence the specialty tea salon operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and corporate name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry NUANS pre-clearance service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Order a NUANS corporate name search report through the Ontario Business Registry or a licensed search house; examine exact matches and confusing similarity with existing Ontario corporations and registered trademarks; ensure the selected name contains a prescribed legal element such as Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, Inc., Corp. or Ltd.; reserve the approved name and record the name search reference number for use with the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report dated within the prior 90 days
Corporate name request letter and brand references
Director and shareholder identification details for the incorporation filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is queried or refused, select a more distinctive modifying word, obtain a fresh NUANS report, and re-submit through the same Ontario Business Registry application; after incorporation, the name can be corrected by Articles of Amendment if a third-party conflict is identified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and file Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation, stating the proposed corporate name, registered office address in Ontario, minimum and maximum number of directors, first director names and residential addresses, the authorized share structure including Class A Common Shares, and any restrictions on the specialty tea salon business. Attach the NUANS report and consent forms, pay the statutory filing fee, and submit electronically; if a federal CBCA incorporation is selected, file ISED Form 4011 with Corporations Canada and then register the corporation extra-provincially in Ontario.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ontario Business Registry issues a deficiency notice, correct the specified field on the portal and resubmit promptly; if the statutory filing is refused, revise the articles or corporate name and file again without losing the original priority date if the amendment is made within the registry cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue Certificate of Incorporation and secure statutory minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Certificate of Incorporation after approval; verify the Ontario Business Identifier Number and the exact legal name; prepare a corporate minute book containing the articles, by-laws, registered office designation, director register, shareholder register, transfer register and specimen share certificates; retain the certificate as prima facie evidence of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book with statutory registers
Blank share certificates and corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error, apply for a certificate of correction through the Ontario Business Registry; if the minute book lacks a statutory form, cure the omission by an organizing board resolution and the execution of corrected registers as soon as discovered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold organizational board meeting and adopt by-laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the first directors; adopt the first board resolution approving the share subscription schedule, registered office address, banking mandate, officer appointments, accounting year-end, execution authorities and the general by-law; document the meeting in formal minutes and place the resolutions and by-law in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation
Consents to act and officer acceptance forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable, pass an unanimous written resolution in lieu of a meeting in accordance with OBCA; if the by-law provision conflicts with the OBCA, amend the by-law by subsequent corporate resolution and file the amendment if required by the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register tax, payroll and municipal business accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Ontario Ministry of Finance / local municipal licensing office / Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a federal Business Number through CRA Business Registration Online; register for GST/HST if taxable supplies will exceed the $30,000 small-supplier threshold, open a payroll deduction account for CPP and EI if employees are hired, and register for Ontario corporate income tax and Employer Health Tax if applicable; apply to the local municipal licensing office for the food premises business licence, zoning and occupancy approvals required to operate the tea salon lounge.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the specialty tea salon premises
GST/HST and payroll account registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA account activation is delayed, contact the CRA business accounts line or use account registration now through Represent a Client; if municipal licensing is queried, submit revised floor plans and address the zoning or building code findings at a pre-licensing inspection and then resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalize statutory corporate records and compliance calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors / Ontario Business Registry / CRA / Ontario Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record the initial share ledgers, issue share certificates to subscribers, update the registered office and director information in the Ontario Business Registry, and file any initial return or annual return required by Ontario; prepare a compliance calendar with annual corporate return deadlines, shareholder meeting dates, GST/HST remittances, payroll remittances, Employer Health Tax payments and municipal licence renewals; maintain the minute book at the registered office or at another place in Canada designated by the board.
required_dossiers: Issued share certificates and securities ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return or director update is rejected by the Ontario Business Registry, re-file through the registry dashboard using the Ontario Business Identifier Number; if the registered office changes, adopt a board resolution and file the notice within the OBCA time limit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Licensing and Standards for the City of Toronto or the applicable Ontario municipality, together with the local public health unit under the Ontario Ministry of Health; Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario if the lounge later introduces beverage alcohol sales.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Specialty Food Premises Operating Licence (Tea Salon Lounge) issued under Ontario Food Premises Regulation O. Reg. 493/17 and the applicable Municipal Business Licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Low Impact - Tea salon operations are generally exempt from a full Environmental Assessment; an Environmental Activity and Sector Registry (EASR) notice may be required only if the premises installs industrial-scale fuel-burning equipment, a wastewater treatment system or other equipment listed under O. Reg. 1/17.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary and wash wastewater must be discharged to the municipal sanitary sewer and comply with the City of Toronto Sewer Use By-law (Municipal Code Chapter 681) or the applicable municipal by-law limits, including temperature not exceeding 40 degrees Celsius, pH within 6.0 to 11.0, and acceptable limits for total suspended solids and oil and grease; commercial exhaust and ventilation must satisfy municipal odour and HVAC make-up air requirements; spent tea leaves must be disposed as organic waste through a licensed waste carrier in compliance with O. Reg. 347/90; any refrigerant or compressor systems must comply with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 for ozone-depleting substances and refrigerants.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance: completion of an annual fire safety inspection and issuance of a fire code compliance letter under the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07), including approved means of egress, fire extinguishers, fire alarm notification, occupancy load calculation, and kitchen suppression coverage for commercial tea brewing equipment; Structural and Occupational Clearance: issuance of a building occupancy permit confirming structural load capacity for salon display shelving and ceramic service areas, and completion of a pre-opening health inspection under O. Reg. 493/17; the employer must register with the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) and comply with the Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act before employees begin work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada; online portals: CRA My Business Account, Business Registration Online, and GST/HST NETFILE
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Canadian corporation must first complete federal or provincial incorporation, then apply for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and GST/HST program account through CRA's Business Registration Online or Form RC1. The application must state the Ontario business address, directors, authorized signatory, expected Canadian taxable supplies, and, for non-resident directors, a Canadian resident agent may be required. CRA issues the BN/RT program account, which serves as the TIN and GST/HST registration number, before taxable commercial activity begins.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style 'check-the-box' election and no hybrid-mismatch entity election; a federally or provincially incorporated Canadian corporation is categorically taxed as a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act. Available elections relate to transactions, not entity classification: GST/HST joint elections under sections 155 to 157 of the Excise Tax Act for closely related persons, section 216 and 217 elections for certain non-resident income, and the GST/HST quick method election for small registrants. None of these alter the default corporate entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (Canada): Goods and Services Tax (GST) combined with Ontario Harmonized Sales Tax (HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000; calculated on worldwide taxable supplies, excluding zero-rated supplies, once the non-resident corporation carries on business in Canada or has a permanent establishment in Ontario. Registration becomes mandatory after exceeding the 30-day or 12-month threshold in a calendar quarter or fiscal year; voluntary registration is available for small suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, pre-approval clearance, or digital stamping is mandated in Canada. GST/HST registrants must issue prescribed tax invoices in paper or electronic form and retain them for audit. Most registrants must file GST/HST returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or CRA-certified software; integrated filers may use CRA's GST/HST Web Services API or XML formats. Invoices are not filed with the CRA before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under sections 1, 2 and 5 of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, a specialty tea salon may zero-rate supplies of tea leaves, tea products, and ceremonial goods only when the goods are physically exported by the supplier or on behalf of the customer as part of the supply, ordinarily within a reasonable time, and the supplier retains clear documentary proof that the goods left Canada. Services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated under section 7 of Schedule VI if the service is performed in Canada but delivered to a non-resident, or where the supply relates to tangible personal property exported from Canada. On-premises tea service and lounge sales remain subject to Ontario HST at the standard rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A / eDeclaration for shipments above the legal reporting threshold)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export from Canada
Customs/external transport record (carrier proof of pick-up and foreign destination)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/foreign exchange transfer record evidencing final payment from the foreign buyer
CBSA release documents or transportation broker reports on vessel/aircraft departure
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may disallow zero-rating if export documentation is incomplete or inconsistent; the full 13% HST is then reassessed on the exporter, with input tax credits clawed back and refunds reversed. Penalties under the Excise Tax Act can include a 6% assessable error amount plus monthly arrears interest, 25% gross negligence penalties, and summary conviction or indictable fines for fraudulent statements, with a retrospective reassessment period extended beyond four years where a taxpayer has made a misrepresentation that is negligent or amounting to fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential supervision of Schedule I banks by OSFI; AML/ATF supervision by FINTRAC
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no foreign exchange controls or restrictions on profit remittances. Dividends, management fees, and royalties may be repatriated freely, subject to ordinary corporate authorization, CRA non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, and the bank's own KYC/AML verification of underlying transaction validity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion requirement exists in Canada. Export receipts for tea inventory, ceramics, or franchise/royalty inflows may be retained in foreign currency or repatriated without central bank approval. The only obligations are commercial invoicing, customs declarations through the CBSA, and FINTRAC reporting for transactions over the statutory threshold.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Business Account / Capital Escrow Account

Operational Business Account / Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Canada has no dedicated 'EMI' banking license. A foreign fintech/EMI offering digital accounts is legally not a substitute for a Schedule I bank; it cannot take deposits unless licensed under the Bank Act. Such an EMI may operate as a money services business registered with FINTRAC, but for cross-border settlement, FX conversion, and Ontario treasury operations, a Schedule I bank remains the primary clearing entity. Foreign EMIs may be acceptable for low-value sales channels, but they create additional compliance risk and are not suitable for capital escrow or trade LC disbursement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In Ontario, a private Ontario corporation with non-resident directors can usually open an account remotely if it appoints a Canadian-resident signing officer or director and provides notarized corporate documents. In practice, most Schedule I banks require at least one in-person interview by the beneficial owner, director, or an authorized Canadian signatory before the account is fully activated. Some banks, including RBC and BMO, offer remote video onboarding for low-risk retail and business clients, but fully digital onboarding without any Canadian nexus or physical presence is rarely granted for companies with foreign parent entities. A physical appearance by a designated Canadian representative is the safest compliance path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or director resident in a FATF-high-risk jurisdiction or with sanctions/PEP exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete source-of-funds and source-of-wealth affidavit, notarized passport copy, proof of address, corporate chart, beneficial ownership registry, professional reference letter, and a clean PEP/sanctions screening report from a recognized compliance vendor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-heavy point-of-sale revenue model for the tea salon without consistent sales records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12 months of historical POS terminal reports, daily sales reconciliation, inventory purchase invoices for tea and ceramics, lease agreement showing commercial foot traffic, and a signed AML declaration explaining the expected cash-to-card ratio.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate third-party inbound transfer from a related/foreign entity without documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed shareholder loan agreement or capital contribution resolution, board minutes authorizing the transfer, audited or reviewed financial statements of the parent, and the bank's mandatory source-of-funds questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office reported as a personal residence or virtual office, creating a 'shell entity' suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease agreement for the tea salon lounge, utility invoices, municipal business license, filmed interior/exterior proof of business operations, and a corporate tax filing showing active operating revenue.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital injections are cleared over the SWIFT network into a Schedule I bank corporate account. No exchange control permit is required. The remitter should use SWIFT MT103 with beneficiary as the Ontario entity, and Field 70 should clearly state 'shareholder capital injection' or 'working capital loan.' The receiving bank will request supporting documents such as the board resolution, shareholder loan agreement, source-of-funds evidence, and confirmation that the transaction does not trigger investment review thresholds under the Investment Canada Act. For a specialty tea salon, a direct capital injection below the review threshold is generally lawful and immediately available after standard KYC verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for imported loose-leaf tea, premium ceramics, or franchise payments should use SWIFT MT103 for lower-value settlement, commercial letters of credit through a Schedule I Canadian bank for high-value inventory purchases, and cross-border card rails for small e-commerce payments. Payment instructions must include the underlying commercial invoice and, where applicable, a clear description of goods. Canada does not require a foreign exchange permit, but the paying bank will screen for sanctions and the beneficiary must be an authorized payee. Outbound wire payments are also subject to CRA withholding assessment if the payment constitutes a dividend, royalty, or management fee to a non-resident.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards with Canadian Schedule I banks for CAD/CNY, CAD/USD, and CAD/EUR exposures
Cross-currency swaps for long-term commercial obligations
FX options for procurement price protection on bulk tea purchases
NDFs are not generally necessary for CAD because the currency is freely convertible; however, OTC NDFs may be permitted for exotic emerging-market trade exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Annual Corporate Return (annual filing under the Corporations Information Act and Ontario Business Corporations Act, confirming registered office, directors, officers, shareholders, and individual(s) with significant control)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Province of Ontario
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date of incorporation each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing levy of CAD 100; failure to file for two consecutive years exposes the corporation to administrative dissolution or strike-off, with reinstatement conditioned on Ministry approval, payment of outstanding fees, and renewed compliance filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and related schedules (federal corporate tax and Ontario provincial corporate tax administered by the CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (acting as tax administrator for the Ontario Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of the corporation's taxation year (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax amount plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months), minimum penalties in the presence of tax payable, and daily compound interest on balances; repeated non-compliance may trigger CRA audit, asset freeze, and director liability assessments for unpaid payroll or income tax withholdings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST return for an annual filer (Ontario HST at 13%, composed of 5% federal and 8% provincial components)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end for an annual filer (e.g., March 31 for a December 31 year-end), with remittance due on the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5% of the amount owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months, daily compound interest on late amounts, and CRA set-off of any tax credits or refunds against arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement of Remuneration Paid and T4 Summary (annual payroll information returns) required where the specialty tea salon lounge employs staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February immediately following each calendar year in which salary, wages, or taxable benefits were paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of at least CAD 100 per T4 information return plus CAD 25 per T4 slip for each day late (maximum CAD 100 per slip); failure to issue employee T4 slips attracts additional penalties and summary conviction prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under OBCA section 148, a non-distributing Ontario corporation must appoint an auditor unless it has fewer than 15 shareholders, gross annual revenue does not exceed CAD 5 million, total assets do not exceed CAD 10 million, and all shareholders unanimously consent in writing to waive the audit at the annual shareholders' meeting; a specialty tea salon corporation satisfying these tests may validly dispense with a statutory audit, otherwise a licensed public accountant must audit the annual financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; private Ontario corporations may adopt Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); the chosen framework must be applied consistently, and the annual financial statements and underlying books and records must be maintained at the registered office for the statutory retention period.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: OBCA requires every Ontario corporation to maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC), update the register within 15 days of any change, and confirm that the register is complete and accurate as of the anniversary date each year; false or incomplete ISC filings expose the corporation to fines up to CAD 200,000 and directors or officers to fines up to CAD 50,000.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute Book containing minutes of shareholder meetings, director meetings, and written resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 to 400 per annum for a registered corporate office address or corporate service agent located in Ontario
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 to 8,000 per annum for a certified Canadian CPA statutory audit; USD 900 to 2,000 per annum for a review engagement where the OBCA audit is validly waived

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general 15% + Ontario general 11.5% = combined 26.5%; for a Canadian-controlled private corporation qualifying for small business deductions, combined effective rate is 12.2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (effective federal rate 9%) and Ontario small business deduction (provincial rate 3.2%) apply only to a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) on active business income up to the shared CAD 500,000 business limit; Ontario M&P credit at 10% does not normally apply to specialty-tea retail service; no other tea-specific sectoral tax holiday.
